solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The gun he left behind? It's nothing

indicators.note: something left behind is dropped and not taken along, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a rifle is a gun

explanation.surface: A detective finds a gun abandoned by a suspect, who shrugs it off as nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he left behind' reads like a gunman fleeing, but it strips two letters from the first word, so only its initial survives.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle is something of little value or importance, a mere nothing.

definitions.meaning: a Panama hat is worn on top, so it is clothing for the head, upper garments

explanation.surface: A quiz asks which television programme could serve as a description of the Panama hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Panama is a straw hat, not the country or canal: 'gear' is clothing and a hat goes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Gear is a British television motoring series; a hat is gear worn at the top of the body.

clue.text: To guard against infection I clean out wound

indicators.note: wound, read as the past of wind, means twisted round, so the letters are coiled into a new order

explanation.surface: First-aid advice: to stop infection, I clean out the wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury but is the anagram signal, from winding.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaccinating someone protects them from catching a disease, the infinitive matching 'To guard'.

clue.text: FBI agent tailing the French errand boy

indicators.note: tailing means following behind, so the agent comes after the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
a G-man is an American slang term for a federal agent

explanation.surface: An FBI agent shadows a Frenchman's messenger boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A legman is someone who runs errands or gathers information on foot for another person.

parts.note: Charles II hid in an oak tree at Boscobel after the battle of Worcester, and many British pubs are named after that tree

explanation.surface: A pub where a man called Charles goes to hide from the world.
explanation.walkthrough: Boozer is British slang for a pub; the Royal Oak is a common pub name commemorating the tree that hid the future Charles II in 1651.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs commonly bear this name, and the original tree sheltered a fleeing king.

clue.text: Rings when dumped by husband? Oh dear

indicators.note: being dumped by someone means they leave, so the husband letter departs

parts.note: hoops are rings

explanation.surface: Wedding rings handed back after a husband walks out: oh dear.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of dismay at a small mistake or mishap.

clue.text: I'm worried, a soldier said, heading off

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: with its heading off the word loses its first letter

parts.note: stated means said

explanation.surface: A soldier reports, sounding anxious, that he is worried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm' has the answer describe itself: 'I'm worried' says the word means worried.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone agitated is anxious and unsettled, a near synonym.

clue.text: Nothing written by congregation in times past

indicators.note: written by means placed beside, so the zero comes next to the flock

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
a fold is a church congregation, a flock

explanation.surface: A church congregation once wrote nothing down.
explanation.definitionFit: Of old is a literary phrase meaning formerly, long ago.

indicators.note: among says the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird among the fastest set free.
explanation.definitionFit: A kestrel is a small falcon, a bird of prey known for hovering.

definitions.meaning: to turn the soil for planting, to till
a group of seven bright stars in Ursa Major, the Big Dipper

explanation.walkthrough: The British name for the Big Dipper is the Plough.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers till fields before sowing; the star group is named after the farm implement.

clue.text: Fruit from American tropics going off

indicators.note: going off suggests fruit spoiling, which here signals the letters going awry

explanation.surface: Imported fruit from the American tropics starting to rot.
explanation.definitionFit: Apricots are orange stone fruits, a plural example of fruit.

clue.text: Pitman increasingly happy with new leader

indicators.note: a new leader means the first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: jollier means happier, more cheerful

explanation.surface: A miner grows more cheerful under a new boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter is the new one; the definition decides it is C.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner, one who works in a pit.

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things happening out of the normal order

explanation.surface: A teacher suddenly dashed out of the classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An educator is a person who instructs others, a synonym for a teacher.

definitions.meaning: having a ... is British slang for taking a look
the male of the goose species

explanation.walkthrough: A gander as a look is informal British usage, as in 'have a gander'.
explanation.definitionFit: The male goose has this name, and the slang phrase means a quick glance.

clue.text: Encourage woman to acquire English guile

indicators.note: to acquire means to take in, so the woman holds the other letters

parts.note: hen is slang for a woman
art means cunning, guile

explanation.surface: A woman is urged to pick up English cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to give them courage, lifting their spirits.

indicators.note: a dictator dictates, speaking words aloud for someone to write down, so the word is given by sound

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A tourist strolls around Mussolini's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dictator's' looks like Mussolini or Caesar, but it signals dictation: the capital spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to travel aimlessly about a place, to drift or rove.

parts.note: blue means smutty or pornographic, as in blue films
a pencil is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A censor bans a writer of pornography.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors used blue crayon to strike out material, so the verb means to cut or suppress.

parts.note: crack means first-rate, as in a crack shot
head is short for head teacher

explanation.surface: A superb schoolteacher who is secretly hooked on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Head is the British short form of headteacher, a school principal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a person dependent on crack cocaine.

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: A member of parliament mocked over his choice of profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun meaning profession but is the verb, to rush headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to charge wildly, as a panicking herd does.

parts.note: the middle letter, or heart, of the word sweet is the letter E, so the two parts read as wordplay supply that letter

explanation.surface: A girlfriend gives you a grade E, or perhaps a little pill.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer split in two works as wordplay producing E.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart is a beloved partner, a term of affection for a lover.

clue.text: Southern peninsula, a place of exile

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A southern peninsula to which people were banished.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia and the Soviet Union sent prisoners and dissidents to this remote region.

definitions.meaning: to couple is to pair or breed
an infusion of a South American holly, drunk as a herbal drink

explanation.surface: A pair of people sharing a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals pair up to breed, and the South American drink is a caffeinated leaf brew.

clue.text: Honour east German city, overthrown and left half-abandoned

indicators.note: overthrown means turned over, so the city is written backwards

parts.note: Bonn is a city in Germany, the former West German capital

indicators.note: half-abandoned keeps only the first half of the word

explanation.surface: An eastern German city falls and is left half deserted, yet it is honoured.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the nobility, conferring an honour.

clue.text: Contract defaced? It makes you cross

indicators.note: defaced means losing its face, the front letter

parts.note: to abridge is to shorten or contract

explanation.surface: A spoiled agreement that leaves you angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' is the verb to shorten, not an agreement; 'cross' is to traverse, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge is a structure allowing people to get over a river or road.

clue.text: Was appointed bishop by reactionary church? Answer me!

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: reactionary means going backwards, so the church letters are reversed

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A bishop of a conservative church is asked whether he was appointed.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming a bishop or mayor is to be made one, to take on a role.

clue.text: Where one might seduce Conservative? That's a sore point

parts.note: ouch is the cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is seduced, and it remains an embarrassing subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is a classic setting for romance, as in the casting couch.

indicators.note: you say means the words are spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: bare means naked; skin is the flesh's outer layer

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the instruction is to cover up exposed skin.
explanation.walkthrough: A bearskin is the tall fur hat of British guards, or a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: The hat covers a guardsman's head; a rug made from the pelt covers a floor.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A doctor notes some unpleasant eye infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid caused by bacterial infection.

indicators.note: to block means to sit in the middle of, so the permission goes inside the path

parts.note: a route is a path
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A game is permitted to obstruct the footpath.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling game with a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Sailor holding vicar back, foolishly perhaps

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the sailor wraps around the other letters

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: back means turned round, read in the reverse order

parts.note: Revd is the abbreviation for Reverend, a vicar's title

explanation.surface: A sailor foolishly holds back a vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly perhaps' defines by example: it is a word of that part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolishly modifies a verb, an example of this part of speech.

indicators.note: running suggests movement, so the letters are put in motion into a new order

explanation.surface: A successful man is in charge of a European archive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' looks like managing the archive but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who accomplishes much is a high-flyer, a winner.

definitions.meaning: a drug addict injects with a hypodermic

explanation.surface: Irritate a drug addict using one.
explanation.definitionFit: Provoking someone is to goad them; a syringe has a sharp point for injecting.
